acceptance.one_rule: shared/sparknet-rfi-install.py owns this order. Every receive path — a live listener and an operator carrying an artifact to a node whose listener is not running — installs through it, so the two cannot disagree about what a peer trusts. A second copy of the order is how the guard-approval rule drifted before Step 5.
order: the source is loopback or the Master's overlay address; anything else is refused before the body is read
the artifact parses and carries exactly the declared fields — an extra field is refused, because a field outside the projection is unsigned
the signature verifies under the registry's master public key
content_sha256 equals the digest of the decoded content_b64
item_name is a single safe component under 01_Inbox/
request_id has not already been installed on this node
only then: write the item, record the request_id, and record an inbox_acceptance block
acceptance.records: Installing an answer writes the item into 01_Inbox/ and appends an inbox_acceptance ledger block with source master-node, which is the event shared/sparknet-provenance.py::build_inbox_acceptance produces. Master-origin material may be executed on notice per tracking-schema.json inbox_dispatch, but it is still recorded: the trail of what arrived is what makes the arrival attributable.
acceptance.write_order: the item is written before the request_id is recorded, so a crash between them re-delivers rather than losing the answer. The reverse order would record an acceptance for an item that never landed, and a ledger claiming a delivery that did not happen is worse than a duplicate.

answer.digest_rule: content_sha256 must equal the sha256 of the bytes content_b64 decodes to. The content itself is not in the signed projection — it is bound by its digest — because an answer can be large and the projection should stay small enough to canonicalise identically everywhere. A digest that disagrees with the payload is refused before the payload is read.
answer.duplicate_rule: A peer records every request_id it has installed. A second answer for one already installed is refused as duplicate_answer, which is what makes re-delivery idempotent and makes replaying an older answer for the same request impossible. There is no global sequence here, unlike the registry publication, because answers are independent items rather than successive states of one document: a registry supersedes, an answer accumulates.
answer.expiry: answered_at plus the peer's inbox policy window. An answer that arrives after it is refused as expired, because information the Master prepared for a question asked days ago may no longer be what the question meant.

item_name.rule: a single path component under 01_Inbox/. It must contain no separator and no '..' — the answer is written into the inbox, so a name that could traverse would write outside it.
item_name.why_signed: It is inside the projection because where an answer lands is part of what the Master authorised. An unsigned name would let a deliverer choose the destination.

peer_fingerprint.why: Binds the answer to the peer it was prepared for. Without it, an answer minted for one node would be a valid answer any node could install into its own inbox, and the material inside it would have crossed a boundary nobody authorised. This is the same reason a guard approval names its peer.

answer.signature_covers: the projection (answered_at, content_sha256, item_name, peer_fingerprint, request_id); the content is bound by content_sha256
answer.signature_travels: beside the fields, in the same artifact; it is not part of the signed projection

description: The request-for-information channel: how a peer asks the Master for information, and how the Master's answer lands in that peer's 01_Inbox. The reference implementation is shared/sparknet-authz.py (the envelope) and shared/sparknet-rfi-install.py (the one acceptance rule); this file is the normative statement of both.

implementation_state.envelope: implemented — shared/sparknet-authz.py signs, projects and verifies
implementation_state.honest_pair: implemented reference code, exercised end to end over a loopback guard in master-node/tests/test_rfi_transport.py (including request -> real 8090 intake -> queued artifact -> composer -> peer 01_Inbox/) and master-node/tests/test_peer_intake.py; nothing is deployed here, and the cross-node leg on a live pair is explicitly a human's to confirm
implementation_state.install_rule: implemented — shared/sparknet-rfi-install.py, exercised in-process and over the wire
implementation_state.listener: implemented (fabric Step 67D) — POST /api/v1/rfi is a third route on the guard's 9090 (peer-node/services/sparknet-guard-d.py::handle_rfi), behind the guard's own source gate, size limit and refusal vocabulary, installing through shared/sparknet-rfi-install.py. contracts/ports.json names the route on 9090, which is what tracking-schema.json's phase_boundary rule requires before transport delivery may be claimed. The route is not gated on the peer's capability, like the registry route: information the Master addressed to this node must reach it.
implementation_state.master_side_composer: implemented (fabric Steps 67D, 70C) — master-node/scripts/sparknet-rfi-answer.sh composes one answer, signs it with the operational key (through the isolated signer's sign-rfi-answer op, or --offline), checks it with the receiver's own rule, resolves the destination peer from the signed registry, and pushes it to the peer's /api/v1/rfi. With --request <artifact> it consumes the file the 8090 peer intake queued: it re-verifies shape and freshness (attribution was the intake's overlay-derived source, not the composer's), takes request_id and peer_fingerprint from the request, and enforces the request's scope against the categories the answer declares with --sources (a non-empty answer must declare them; any outside the scope is refused, so scope narrows and never widens). Declaring sources is the upstream gatherer's attestation; content provenance beyond that is not something this channel can verify. The --request-id/--peer operator path remains for out-of-band requests. `make -C master-node rfi-answer` runs it.
implementation_state.request_channel: implemented (fabric Step 70B) — POST /api/v1/rfi-request is a sibling route on the Master's 8090 peer-intake (master-node/services/sparknet-peer-intake.py). It shares the registry source gate but requires no capability: registered and not revoked is the whole gate, because asking a question is not reporting evidence. 68A's attribution (RFI_REQUEST_DESIGN.md) stands — authz.verify_rfi_request checks shape, the overlay-derived fingerprint match, freshness and nonce replay, and there is no signature to check. An accepted request is written as one content-addressed JSON artifact (0600) under /mnt/log/sparknet-rfi-requests for the composer; the route never answers it and cannot widen scope. The composer's --request consumption is implemented in Step 70C: it re-verifies shape/freshness, takes the peer and id from the artifact, and refuses any --sources category outside the request's scope.
implementation_state.responder: built with the user-node step — master-node/services/sparknet-rfi-responder.py consumes queued requests, searches only the allow-listed fabric corpus, enforces the request scope, returns an empty answer when nothing matches, and delegates signing/delivery to scripts/sparknet-rfi-answer.sh --request. The unit is staged, not enabled; a live cross-node answer remains DoD: confirm: user.
implementation_state.signer_op: implemented (fabric Step 67D) — master-node/services/sparknet-signer.py answers sign-rfi-answer, deriving content_sha256 from the payload rather than trusting a caller-supplied digest, so the isolated key holder signs the answer the same way it signs a registry publication.

refusals.bad_signature: the signature does not verify under the registry's master public key
refusals.digest_mismatch: content_sha256 is not the digest of the decoded content
refusals.duplicate_answer: this request_id is already installed here
refusals.expired: the answer arrived after its window
refusals.extra_fields: a field outside the declared envelope, which would be unsigned authority-shaped data
refusals.malformed: the artifact is not JSON, or is not an object
refusals.off_overlay: the source is neither loopback nor the Master's overlay address
refusals.unsafe_item_name: item_name traverses or names a subdirectory

request.attribution: the authenticated overlay, NOT a signature — decided in RFI_REQUEST_DESIGN.md (fabric Step 68A). The Master receives the request on an overlay-only listener, derives the sender's fingerprint from the WireGuard-authenticated source address via its own registry (overlay_ipv4 -> fingerprint), and refuses a request whose peer_fingerprint field disagrees. A node-key signature was the original 67C plan but is unverifiable: nothing binds a peer fingerprint to a node signing public key, so on the overlay the tunnel is the identity.
request.request_id_rule: stable handle chosen by the requester, unique per peer. The answer echoes it, and it is what makes a re-delivered answer detectable as a duplicate rather than as new information.
request.scope: an allow-list of vault categories the answer may draw on. The Master refuses to answer a request whose scope reaches material the peer is not granted; scope narrows, it never widens. The request channel carries no authority — it cannot grant, revoke, escalate or widen a permission.
request.transport: peer -> Master on the Master's overlay-only listener on 8090 (re-scoped from the superseded instant-push; resolves Master Step 7's open question). Source-gated to registered, non-revoked peer overlay addresses. The listener is master-node/services/sparknet-peer-intake.py; the route is POST /api/v1/rfi-request (fabric Step 70B).
request.unsigned: the request body carries no signature_b64. A signature the Master has no attested key to verify is theatre; attribution rides the tunnel the Master itself terminates and authenticated. nonce + expires_at give the replay protection a signed envelope's freshness fields would.
request.upgrade_path: if node-key non-repudiation is ever required, Option C attests node_pubkey_b64 in the signed envelope (a two-repo change — Python here and Go in goSpark — riding the re-sign already pending from Step 66) and the request gains a signature verified against it. That is additive, not a reshape. See RFI_REQUEST_DESIGN.md.
request.verify: shared/sparknet-authz.py::verify_rfi_request — a validator + fingerprint match, not a signature check: it takes the overlay-derived expected_fingerprint and returns (ok, reason) after checking the exact field set, the fingerprint match, expiry and the nonce. There is deliberately no sign_rfi_request.

transport.body: the answer artifact, JSON; no wrapper and no second signature — the answer is self-authenticating
transport.implementation_state: implemented — the guard serves POST /api/v1/rfi (peer-node/services/sparknet-guard-d.py::handle_rfi) and installs through shared/sparknet-rfi-install.py; the Master-side composer is master-node/scripts/sparknet-rfi-answer.sh
transport.note: The guard's existing port, which already carries two routes (critical-file/patch and registry). A third route on it adds no transport edge and no new attack surface: the source gate, the size limit and the refusal vocabulary are the guard's, and the answer's own signature is checked by the shared install rule.
transport.source_gate: loopback and the Master's overlay address (10.100.0.1); every other source is refused 403 off_overlay before the body is read

why: Intake has to be attributable and replay-proof, or a node cannot tell an answer the Master signed from one somebody wrote into its inbox. The shape is deliberately the registry publication's — a signed projection, a digest-bound payload, and one install rule shared by every receive path — because that channel is built, tested and deployed, and a second invention would be a second thing to get wrong.
